Consult Summary:
26-year-old man with known asthma presents with 3 h history of chest tightness, mild shortness of breath, wheeze, and non-productive cough following recent viral URI; ran out of controller and reliever inhalers.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Chest tightness × 3 h; mild SOB; wheezy, non-productive cough persisting after last week’s cold.  
• Worse on exertion (stairs); no chest pain, no SOB at rest.  
• Past medical history: Asthma (hospitalized/intubated age ≈ 16-17); allergic rhinitis/hay-fever; childhood eczema; childhood milk-protein allergy (resolved).  
• Allergies: Dust; no drug allergies.  
• Medications: Salbutamol inhaler (Ventolin) – ran out, dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  Clenil Modulite steroid inhaler – ran out, dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  Spacer owned “somewhere,” rarely used.  
• Family history: Mother eczema; father asthma.  
• Social / preventive: University student; no details on smoking/alcohol; no recent peak-flow readings; seeks reassurance about safety.

Examination:
(No examination or vitals documented.)

Impression:
Likely mild/moderate asthma exacerbation triggered by recent viral URI and non-adherence due to lack of inhalers.

Plan:
• Prescribe Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler.  
• Prescribe Clenil Modulite (beclomethasone) inhaler for regular use; continue once exacerbation settles.  
• Oral corticosteroid course: “two tablets in the morning for 5 days” (exact drug/dose not documented). Counsel on common side-effects (mood change, hyperglycemia, rash, nausea, headache).  
• Issue new spacer device and provide technique instructions.  
• Education:  
  – Use Ventolin PRN; seek medical review if requiring it more often than every 3 h or if symptoms worsen (increasing SOB, chest tightness, light-headedness).  
  – Rest; time off work/university as needed (can self-certify ≤7 d).  
• Arrange prescription delivery “within the hour.”  
• Safety-net: Attend urgent care/ED if deterioration.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected: Smoking status, alcohol use, objective vitals, peak-flow or lung exam, complete steroid prescription details, formal asthma action plan, vaccination status.  
● No internal conflicts identified.  
● Transcript quality acceptable; minor audio dropouts but clinically adequate.
